manual_sample.result: All 60 sampled resolutions are correct on title, first author, year and venue. All 242 RESOLVED_BIBLIOGRAPHIC records pass my independent title test (an exact letters substring, or at least 80% word coverage). All of them come from styles that print titles; Man, Garcia-Mota and Lee never reach RESOLVED_BIBLIOGRAPHIC. Every chosen bibliographic item is the ranked item in the saved raw query response and has four-field agreement. No resolved record is a correction or erratum: all 346 are journal-article, and none is titled Correction or Erratum.

findings.detail: The Limits text says 'Lim's five and Lee's supplementary files are still inaccessible'. That is now out of date: the parallel supplement_access folder reports all five Lim files and the Lee SI as CLOSED, and I verified them below. Leaving the Lee SI's 9 references out of this link set is correct for this pass, but the text should say they were obtained and are not yet linked.

This record is RESOLVED_BIBLIOGRAPHIC to 10.1038/s41467-022-34464-6, a developmental-biology paper on pancreatic fibroblasts. The resolution is faithful: Feng's own bibliography prints that citation, so the off-topic citation is in the source. It is not a false resolution, but it is worth knowing before any screening.

The printed citation reads 'Energy Environ. Sci. 2025, 493, No. 144933'; the Crossref record 10.1039/d4ee03084b has volume 18, pages 6456-6529. Title, first author, year and journal all agree, so the four-field rule is met, and the record is flagged NEITHER_VOLUME_NOR_PAGE_AGREES. The printed volume and article number look borrowed from another work. The exact title match still supports the identity well.

The CONFLICT is correctly kept. The printed DOI 10.1021/jacs.5b07788 is Reier et al. The printed citation (Wang et al., Co-doped FeS2, JACS 2015, 137, 1587) is confirmed only as supplementary_bibliographic_evidence (10.1021/ja511572q), and that DOI is not counted among the resolved DOIs. This is conservative and follows the rules.

Both stay at CANDIDATE_MATCHED_CORRECTION_OR_ERRATUM_NOTICE even though the item has four-field agreement, because the match is the 'Correction to' notice 10.1021/cr4003853. This is the correct use of the erratum guard.
The file has 733 lines for 731 request keys: works:10.5281/zenodo.12635 appears three times, once per run, each a 404. All three 404 bodies are kept and match their hashes. The README discloses this.

could_not_verify: I did not check the 168 CANDIDATE and 9 UNRESOLVED records for missed identities. They claim no identity, so they cannot be false resolutions.
I compared only 8 saved Crossref records with live Crossref. I checked the other raw bodies against their receipt hashes but did not fetch them again.
I checked that the 41 cache-reused bodies are byte-equal to their cache sources and that the cache receipt files exist. I did not re-audit how those caches were originally retrieved.
I did not check that the 2026-09-20/21 transcriptions match the source PDFs, except for Lee, which folder 2 covers.

findings.detail: The recorded hashes 5480969805d917d9... (SI block) and 656665484cf5b8cb... (article block) do not match the files on disk (af745c2139eaa81d..., e340e30ef50ea9b6...). verify.py hashed the in-memory text, which has LF line endings, but write_text on Windows wrote CRLF (37 and 120 CRLFs). Converting the disk bytes from CRLF to LF reproduces the recorded hashes exactly, so the content is intact. A byte-level hash check will still report a mismatch. Fix: hash the bytes as written, or write with newline='\n'. These are the only hash mismatches in the folder.
The Lim section records no licence field, although the README says both works are CC BY. The saved bodies do support CC BY 4.0 (Crossref, Unpaywall, figshare).
The 403 bodies are Cloudflare 'Just a moment...' bot-challenge pages, not publisher paywall refusals. 'Failed' is still the right status; the cause is a challenge to automated clients.

verify.py reads the declared Lim file list from results/s2_2026-09-21/primary_access/lim_xml_links.json, which is outside this folder. I confirmed the list independently from the saved publisher HTML body inside this folder.

The 4th sample is stored with ExtraSamples=0 (unspecified), so PIL decodes RGB only and the image looks black. Compositing sample 4 as alpha makes the captions legible, which confirms the producer's description.

could_not_verify: I could not compare the Lee SI or article with Wiley's own bytes, because every Wiley route is blocked by Cloudflare (the producer reports the same limit). The identification rests instead on two independent PMC copies plus the PMC md5, and on the PuRe publisher-version checksum.

I could not confirm that the files on the Frontiers figshare portal are byte-identical to what frontiersin.org would serve, because the publisher's component URLs return the article HTML, not files. The identification rests on figshare's resource_doi, the component DOIs, the Crossref component titles and the captions.
I read the TIF captions visually from the composited images; I did not run OCR.
The DOCX checks used the raw XML text; I did not check page rendering or layout.
I did not inspect Lee SI pages 2-13 beyond the page count; I read only the title page and page 14 (the references).
